what_worked: Strong thesis (crowded ≠ lucrative) carried consistently through every slide with honest caveats on small samples.
fix_next: Median revenue figures appear to be annualized (×12) without disclosure; the dataset reports 30-day revenue, so state your transformation or use the raw metric.
verdict: Coherent category story undermined by silently annualized medians and some unverifiable figures.
factual_error_detail: Slide 2: 'Median 12-mo revenue' values appear to be 30-day medians × 12 but are presented as observed data without disclosing the multiplication (e.g., Education $14.3K ≈ $2,435×~5.9 or Content Creation $13,733 ≈ $1,237.50×11.1—neither cleanly ×12). Marketing shown as $10,029 vs reference median $2,369.50 (×4.2, not ×12). The multipliers are inconsistent across categories, suggesting either fabrication or a different unreported calculation. Slide 3: Education '$14.3K median 12-mo rev' and Content Creation '$13.7K' carry forward the same problematic figures. Slide 3: 'Sales' category with 13 listings and $8.2K median is not in the frozen reference set—cannot verify. Slide 2: AI median shown as $4,301; reference 30-day median is $503 (×8.6, not ×12). Slide 4: Rev/customer figures for Sales ($103), Marketing ($54), etc. are unverifiable derived metrics with no formula shown.

evidence.insight: Slide 2 delivers a genuinely useful 'crowded ≠ lucrative' insight comparing AI's 197 companies to its low median. Slide 4 adds per-customer value with an honest caveat about Sales' tiny n=13. Slide 6 distinguishes reliable vs unreliable signals. These go beyond chart description.
evidence.narrative: Clear arc: problem (AI overcrowded) → alternatives (Education/Content/Marketing) → operational setup (Slide 5) → signal quality (Slide 6) → summary recommendations (Slide 7). Each slide builds on the prior. The thesis lands cleanly.
evidence.framing: Audience is implicitly a newcomer choosing a category, stated on Slide 1. However, 274 missing category values (27.4% of data) are never mentioned. No discussion of survivorship bias or what the 216 zero-revenue companies mean for median interpretation. Scope is clear but limitations are thin.
evidence.accuracy: The central issue: median values labeled '12-mo revenue' don't consistently match reference 30-day medians × 12. AI: $4,301 vs $503×12=$6,036. Marketing: $10,029 vs $2,369.50×12=$28,434. Education: $14,300 vs $2,435×12=$29,220. Content Creation: $13,733 vs $1,237.50×12=$14,850. The numbers don't match any single consistent transformation. Company counts (197 AI, 66 SaaS, 52 Mobile Apps, 42 Marketing, 36 Content Creation, 34 Health & Fitness, 30 Education) all match reference. 'Sales' category with 13 companies is not in the reference but may exist in the data.
evidence.visual: Slide 2's dual-axis chart (bars + line) is clearly labeled and annotated. Slide 3's card layout is clean and scannable. Slide 5's table is well-structured. Slide 6's trust/skeptical split is effective. Consistent color palette throughout. No decorative-but-meaningless graphics. Minor issue: Slide 2 line chart connects categorical data, which is misleading.
